newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says probe in Telekom-Ericsson case urgent.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says probe in Telekom-Ericsson case urgent.

text.p: Malaysia has ordered an urgent probe into alleged discrepancies in a contract awarded by Telekom Malaysia to Sweden's Ericsson, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim was quoted as saying on Saturday.
"I have asked for it (the probe) to be speeded up," Anwar said, the national Bernama news agency reported.
"It is not necessary to take too much time because all the records are still there. I have classified it as an urgent matter," he told a news conference.
Anwar, also Malaysia's finance minister, said on Wednesday he had received a report that there may have been "discrepancies" in a tender awarded by state telephone firm Telekom to Ericsson.

He did not say which contract was under question. On Saturday he said the contract was "a case of four of five years ago", adding that the probe should serve as a lesson to all parties not to regard tender awards as insignificant.
"We should be transparent. If there is any report (of discrepancies), we should take it up," he said.
Anwar said the finance ministry, the final approval authority for government contracts, will check if all procedures had been adhered in the contract.
He declined to comment on speculation that some cabinet ministers and senior officials of Telekom may have had a hand in the alleged discrepancies.
Telekom chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali said on Thursday he considered the allegations serious. He added that the company "will do everything in its power to get to the truth".
Ericsson said it suspected the charges were connected to earlier rumours of alleged criminal and unethical action by the company in the Middle East.
"These reports have been spread all over the world, including Malaysia," Ericsson's head of information Lars Stalberg told Reuters in Stockholm.
